clue.text: Get into funk? There's jive that's playing

indicators.note: the letters are playing about, i.e. moved freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the jive being danced looks nervy and jumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of that's stands for 'is' and links fodder to indicator. 'Funk' here is the old sense of fear or panic, not the music the jive suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a funk is to be in a state of nervous fear, so getting into one is becoming anxious and shaky.

clue.text: Figure in clothing for hockey showing cheek in post-match activity

indicators.note: the figure sits inside the clothing formed by the outer letters
the outside letters of hockey are its clothing, wrapping round what goes in

parts.note: one is a figure, a number
mooning is baring one's buttocks, showing a cheek

explanation.surface: A rowdy hockey player in kit bares his backside in the celebrations after the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'match' is a marriage, not a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymoon is the holiday after a wedding, a match in the sense of a marriage, so honeymooning follows it.

clue.text: Very wrong to drink drop of Glenfiddich, a couple of fingers

indicators.note: the word for wrong swallows the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny bit, here just the first letter

explanation.surface: Drinking whisky is a terrible sin, someone suggests, and a measure is two fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Two fingers is a pub measure of whisky, which the surface plays on; the gesture is a British insult made with the index and middle fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: The British rude gesture is made by raising two fingers in a V with the back of the hand outwards.

clue.text: Display extravagant pictures around Roman establishment?

indicators.note: turned around, the whole string is read the other way

parts.note: to air something is to display it
OTT, over the top, means extravagant
art is pictures collectively

explanation.surface: Showy paintings are hung around some building in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the Roman here is a modern Italian, not a citizen of the empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is a simple Italian restaurant, the kind of eating place found in Rome.

clue.text: Wow, one's usurped by English ruler …

indicators.note: one letter's place is seized by another, as a throne is usurped

parts.note: to wow someone is to impress them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dazzling ruler is overthrown by an English one, the ellipsis carrying the story on.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female sovereign, ruling an empire.

clue.text: … whose domains are mostly measured in yards?

indicators.note: most of the word, the final letter left off

parts.note: the imperial system of measures uses yards, feet and inches

explanation.surface: Following on from the empress, it asks whether her lands are reckoned in old British units.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the empress before it: her domains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin plural of imperium, an empire or realm of command, so territories under rule.

clue.text: Addressing Kelly with firmness

parts.note: a letter addressed to someone is written 'to' them
Ned Kelly was the Australian outlaw

explanation.surface: Someone speaks firmly to a person called Kelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ned Kelly was a famous nineteenth-century Australian bushranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned muscles are firm and tight, so the word describes a body that has firmness.

clue.text: Soldiers leading manoeuvres given another order

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: the letters are put through manoeuvres, shifted into a new position

explanation.surface: Troops at the front of exercises are issued a fresh command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a military command, but here it means arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To realign is to arrange again in a line, putting things into a fresh arrangement.

clue.text: Element of Rastafarianism back in African capital

indicators.note: read back, from right to left
an element is a part, so the letters lie within the word

explanation.surface: Part of Rastafarian belief harks back to an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city; it is money, the currency of Nigeria.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is Nigeria's currency, and capital means money.

clue.text: Visit judge, ever the foppish fellow

parts.note: to pop in is to make a brief visit
ay (or aye) is an old word for ever, always

explanation.surface: Someone calls on a judge who has always been a dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A popinjay is a vain, showily dressed man, a dandy or coxcomb.

clue.text: Rappers cross about critics

indicators.note: turned about, the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix
knockers are people who criticise

explanation.surface: Hip-hop artists get angry about the reviewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rappers' suggests musicians; it means things that rap on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: A door knocker is a hinged metal piece used to rap on a door to announce a caller.

clue.text: Fizzy tangy energy drinks unknown for long-distance runner

indicators.note: the outer letters drink in the unknown, holding it inside
fizzing letters bubble about into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A marathon runner takes sharp-tasting fizzy energy drinks of uncertain make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete; it is a river, which runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is China's great river, among the longest in the world, and rivers run.

clue.text: Staff fix round for Spaniard who worked in bars

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
to rig is to fix dishonestly
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A barman from Spain is accused of fixing a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Joaquín Rodrigo was the Spanish composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez; the bars are of music, not pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music in bars, so the Spanish composer worked in them.

clue.text: Edible mollusc men found by sea abroad

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers or men
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: Fishermen find a shellfish by the sea in a foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: The ormer is a Channel Islands name for the abalone.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an abalone, a sea snail eaten as a delicacy, especially in Guernsey.

clue.text: Traveller's car crashed into second car

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the short time

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked, its letters mixed up

parts.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen model of car

explanation.surface: A tourist's car has smashed into another vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian merchant famed for his journey to China, the archetypal explorer.

clue.text: Queen Victoria maybe is first in shop

indicators.note: the London terminus comes first, ahead of the queen

parts.note: Victoria is a London railway station, an example of one
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria is said to come first in some shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs Queen with Victoria, but they part: Victoria is the station and the Queen is ER, which goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a seller of paper and pens, and the name is used for the shop itself.

clue.text: Muslim leader, not a current president, one unfairly scapegoated by tabloids?

indicators.note: not a means the letter a is left out

parts.note: an imam leads prayers in a mosque
I is the physics symbol for electric current
Ulysses S. Grant was a US president

explanation.surface: A cleric, a president, and a person the press like to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcomers from abroad are a frequent target of sensational British newspapers, blamed for social ills.

clue.text: Opera with a lot of musical backing using standards

parts.note: Norma is the opera by Bellini

indicators.note: backing means read backwards
a lot of, not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A production of an opera leans heavily on a musical backing track to meet the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Normative means prescribing or relating to norms, judging by set rules and benchmarks.

clue.text: Almost slight case of indigestion? This affects metabolism

indicators.note: almost all of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a slight is an insult

indicators.note: the case is the outside, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A mild bout of indigestion might, it suggests, be a sign of the body's chemistry at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests an instance of illness; it is the word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone that regulates blood sugar, central to how the body processes food.

clue.text: Picaroon picked up cat hair

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, heard rather than seen

parts.note: the setter, Picaroon, refers to himself as I
to cat is an old term for flogging with a cat-o'-nine-tails, a lash

explanation.surface: The setter notices a cat hair on their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name; here Picaroon means 'I', which sounds like EYE. The cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails whip.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelash is one of the short hairs growing from the edge of the eyelid.

clue.text: Place for Fielding novel's opening — love dark twists

indicators.note: the string twists round to read the other way
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, an O
dim means dark

explanation.surface: The start of a novel by Henry Fielding has a love story taking dark twists.
explanation.walkthrough: Fielding looks like the novelist of Tom Jones; it is the cricket sense. Mid-on is a fielding position near the bowler on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, mid-on is a fielding position on the leg side, close to the bowler.

clue.text: Asian dietary staple: jam sandwiches to start with

parts.note: musicians noodle when they jam, improvising casually

indicators.note: just the letter at the start of the word

explanation.surface: A list of foods: a staple of Asian diets, and jam sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jam' looks like fruit preserve; it is the musical sense, improvising.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles made from wheat or rice are a basic food across much of East and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Races through the smallest room in house

indicators.note: the races run through the room, sitting inside it

parts.note: the smallest room is a jokey name for the toilet, the loo
TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

explanation.surface: Someone dashes through the toilet of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: House (or housey-housey) is an old British name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance like bingo, which British players also call house.

clue.text: Prompt about catching one on dope, aiming for a better race?

indicators.note: the outer word catches the rest, holding them inside
turned about, read backwards

parts.note: a cue prompts an actor

indicators.note: in an across clue one goes on, after, the dope

parts.note: gen is information, as is dope
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A coach urges an athlete caught taking drugs, hoping for a faster run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Race' looks like a sprint; it is the human race, improved by selective breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugenics is the discredited doctrine of improving the human population by controlled breeding.

clue.text: Dives from a board, initially cracking head

indicators.note: the letters crack into the head, splitting it open

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone diving off a board cracks their head.
explanation.walkthrough: Dives is the name traditionally given to the rich man in the parable of Lazarus, not a plunge into water.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a very wealthy man, and Dives is the rich man of the biblical parable.

clue.text: Fare from Mexico is wrong — I'm going to America

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
I'll is short for I will, I'm going to

explanation.surface: Someone declares the Mexican food is bad and they are off to the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flatbread of maize or wheat, a staple of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: What walkers do better stripped off

indicators.note: with the outer layer stripped off, only the inside letters stay

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: Ramblers are said to do better without their clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective; it is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, leisurely pace, as strollers do.

clue.text: Lord has to welcome London Transport's founder

parts.note: the Lord is God

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the other piece sits inside

parts.note: owns means has
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: A peer welcomes the man who founded London's transport network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founder' looks like a person who sets something up; it is the verb meaning to fail or sink.
explanation.definitionFit: To founder is to collapse or fail, and to go down the tubes is an idiom for being ruined.
